author: @FrankCurzio
text:
The CEO of $META just told you the easiest way to get RICH.

Buy the companies supplying Meta’s AI bottlenecks.

Here are 7 I'd buy right now:
media_note: video with content about Meta AI

author: @FrankCurzio
text:
3. Dell ( $DELL ) - $503

Dell builds the servers that go inside AI data centers.

My sources who build these data centers say almost all the new ones use Dell & Super Micro.

It's 15% off its highs. We own it, and I think it's an easy double from here.

author: @FrankCurzio
text:
4. Micron ( $MU ) - $929.76

Micron makes the memory chips every AI system needs. You can't run a GPU without it.

Demand is off the charts, yet it trades at about 5x forward earnings and sits 26% off its highs.

These AI selloffs keep turning into gifts.

author: @FrankCurzio
text:
5. Vertiv ( $VRT ) - $208.80

It makes the cooling & power gear that keeps AI data centers from melting down.

My sources say that gear is SOLD OUT for 2-3 years. Meta, Amazon & Microsoft bought up the production in advance.

It reports earnings tomorrow.

author: @FrankCurzio
text:
6. VivoPower ( $VIVO ) - $2.69

Cheap Nordic power & data center sites it rents to AI companies. 2GW+ of potential in 5-7 years.

Last week it signed a deal with the UAE's Open Innovation AI for sovereign AI data centers.

Market cap: $86M. I added more.

author: @FrankCurzio
text:
7. Digi Power X ( $DGXX ) - $2.38

It owns its data centers AND the power behind them.

A 10-year, $1.1B deal with Cerebras for its Alabama site... and the whole company is worth $243M.

The CEO also spoke at my conference yesterday, scroll down my X to see part of the interview.

author: @KimizqSmile
text:
Honestly, $GOOGL is one of the most interesting stocks to watch right now.

The AI race is getting more competitive, but I don't think the story is just about who has the best model. I'm watching whether Alphabet can turn AI demand into real revenue while keeping costs under control.

Strong growth is great, but valuation and cash flow matter too.

Would you buy $GOOGL at these levels, or wait for more clarity?
